Hey! Marcus from Mozilla.org here! Thank you for sharing interest in the hackathon!
Before beginning, please star the Otari repo, it helps! https://github.com/mozilla-ai/otari
# Welcome to MozFest's Developers Wilding: Online!
Watch this short welcome video: https://youtu.be/6B0Nqao86zE
## What is MozFest's Developers Wilding: Online?
It's a two-week online hackathon that kicks off October 28th (the same starting day as MozFest in Barcelona) and ends November 11th.
# Prizes:
1st: $1,000 + 3 hours with Mozilla.ai engineers
2nd: $200 + 2 hours with Mozilla.ai engineers
3rd: 1 hour with the Mozilla.ai engineers
Use your time with the Mozilla AI engineers to get mentoring, ask questions about your project, and receive feedback from experts!
# What do we do at this hackathon?
Finish your side projects using Otari!
This online hackathon encourages you to finish any side projects you have with the requirement that you use Otari.ai as your hosted AI gateway.
# What is Otari?
Otari by Mozilla AI is an open-source AI infrastructure platform that lets you build applications and agents with the models you choose, including open-weight models.
With capabilities like code execution, web search, and the ability to connect your own tools, Otari helps you build powerful AI agents without being locked into a single frontier AI provider.
For this hackathon, you'll use the hosted platform at Otari.ai. And because Otari is open source, you can always run it on your own infrastructure after the hackathon.
# How do I Sign Up and Participate?
- Sign up through DoraHacks with this info: your name or pseudonym; the email you will use to sign up Otari.ai; one sentence explaining your project
- Sign up for the hosted Otari platform at Otari.ai. The first 200 people to sign up get $20 in tokens.
- Join our Mozilla OSAI Discord and grant yourself the devs-wilding role.
- Please star the Otari repo in GitHub!
- Start a new branch in your project and start building with Otari.ai!
# Hackathon Rubric
Read through the rubric here (linked document, reproduced below)
MozFest Developers Wilding Online Judging Rubric
SCORING OUT OF 100 POINTS
30 Open-weight models | 60 Otari features | 10 Project and demo
1. Open-weight models (30 points)
* 20 points: The project meaningfully uses at least one open-weight model.
* 10 additional points: The project uses two or more open-weight models for different purposes.
2. Otari features (up to 60 points)
10 points for each advanced capability demonstrated, up to the category limit.
Feature | Points
Model routing and fallbacks | 10
MCP integrations | 10
Web search or web fetch | 10
Code execution | 10
Budgets and spending limits | 10
Multiple models serving distinct roles | 10
Guardrails | 10
Per-user budgets | 10
Participants can combine capabilities to reach the 60-point maximum. A feature only earns points when it is actually used in the application, not simply enabled in the dashboard.
3. Project and demonstration (10 points)
* 5 points: The application works and demonstrates a real use case.
* 5 points: The video clearly explains how Otari was integrated and demonstrates the claimed capabilities.
Video demonstration and video feedback cannot use AI. It must be a screen recording with audio of the hackathon participant demonstrating their project.
# Hackathon Submission Requirements:
DEADLINE: Nov 11th 11:59PM TO SUBMIT YOUR PROJECT
- Project name, email address you signed up to Otari.ai, and one line on what your project does
- Public GitHub repository link + the hackathon branch name
- You must use Otari.ai in your project. Please link to the first commit on that branch where Otari came in.
- Otari features used (see the rubric for a list of features)
- Any PRs or issues opened on the Otari repo
- Link to 3-5-min project demo video - Show us the progress you made with Otari!
- Feedback - Please submit either screen recording feedback, written feedback, or both! Please note, video demonstration and video feedback cannot use AI. It must be a screen recording with audio of the hackathon participant demonstrating their project.
  - Link to 3-5-min Otari feedback screen recording answering: What did you build with Otari, and which features did you use? What worked well? What didn't work? What's missing, and what would you change?
  - Written feedback answering: When were you most tempted to skip Otari and call the provider directly? What did you end up building yourself that Otari should've done for you? If the rules hadn't required Otari, would you have continued using Otari?
If your submission does not include these items, you will not be eligible for prizes.
If you have any questions, join the Discord and tag @Marcus.

ideas.title: OpenAudit Agent
ideas.pitch: For indie developers and open-source maintainers overwhelmed by dependency risks, OpenAudit Agent is a security auditor bot that scans GitHub repos via Otari, uses open-weight models to analyze code for vulnerabilities, and generates fix suggestions. The demo wow moment: a single click triggers full repo analysis with CVE detection, fallback reasoning paths, and automated PR suggestions — all powered by routed open models.
ideas.rationale: Uses two open-weight models (CodeLlama for code fixes, DeepSeek-Coder for vulnerability detection) with meaningful roles. Leverages model routing, fallbacks, code execution, web fetch (for CVE databases), guardrails, and per-user budgets — 6 features. Working demo with clear Otari integration in video.

ideas.title: Wilding Tutor
ideas.pitch: A self-hostable AI tutor for Mozilla contributors learning Rust and WebAssembly, using Otari to route between specialized open models for explanations, code generation, and error debugging. The demo wow moment: the agent debugs a real-time WASM compilation error, runs the fix in Otari's code executor, and fetches MDN docs — all while enforcing budget caps per learner.
ideas.rationale: Uses Phi-3 for teaching logic and Starling-LM for error interpretation — two open models with distinct roles. Implements model routing, code execution, web search, guardrails, and budgets. Demo shows real use case with Otari integration clearly explained.

ideas.title: PatchPilot
ideas.pitch: For solo devs shipping side projects, PatchPilot is an autonomous bug-fix agent that monitors GitHub issues, uses Otari to route natural language to open models for root cause analysis, then executes testable fixes. The demo wow moment: it reproduces a bug in a Flask app, writes a fix using CodeLlama, validates it with Otari's code execution, and opens a draft PR — autonomously.
ideas.rationale: Combines Mistral and CodeLlama for intent vs. code tasks. Uses routing, fallbacks, code execution, web fetch (for repo context), guardrails, and per-user budgets. Strong demo with real-world workflow and Otari commit trace.

ideas.title: Open-Source Code Mentor
ideas.pitch: A solo developer struggles to adopt best practices in unfamiliar languages. This Otari-powered agent reviews code snippets, explains issues using open-weight models, and suggests improvements with live web search for documentation. The demo shows a broken Python async function being debugged and fixed in real time with citations from Stack Overflow.
ideas.rationale: Uses Llama 3 and CodeLlama via Otari for explanation and repair (20 pts +10 bonus). Leverages model routing, web fetch, code execution, guardrails, per-user budgets, and multiple models in distinct roles (60 pts). Working demo with clear Otari integration video (10 pts).

ideas.title: Privacy-First Research Assistant
ideas.pitch: A researcher needs fast, private summaries of trending papers without leaking queries to closed APIs. The agent pulls arXiv abstracts, summarizes them using Mistral and Llama 3 via Otari, and enforces budget guardrails. The demo wow moment: summarizing a sensitive preprint with inline citations — all without sending raw text to third-party providers.
ideas.rationale: Uses Mistral and Llama 3 for summarization and classification (30 pts). Implements web fetch, model routing, guardrails, budgets, and multiple models in roles (50 pts). Strong demo showing Otari as privacy enforcer (10 pts).

ideas.title: Local Food Forager
ideas.pitch: Urban foragers want to identify edible plants safely and sustainably. This agent combines image classification (via code execution with OpenELM) and location-based web search to verify species and legality. The demo wow moment: snapping a photo of a wild mushroom, running it through a local model, then fetching regional foraging laws — all within Otari’s sandbox.
ideas.rationale: Uses OpenELM and Llama 3 for vision and reasoning (30 pts). Uses code execution, web search, model routing, guardrails, per-user budgets, and multiple models (60 pts). Real-world use case with compelling demo (10 pts).

ideas.title: Personal Research Assistant with Multi-Model Synthesis
ideas.pitch: A solo developer or researcher overwhelmed by scattered information can use this agent to ask a complex question, have it search the web via Otari, fetch and summarize multiple sources using an open-weight model like Llama 3, then generate a structured report with code execution for data analysis. The demo wow moment: showing the agent answer 'What are the latest trends in renewable energy?' and produce a markdown report with charts from live data.
ideas.rationale: Uses at least one open-weight model (Llama 3) for summarization and another (e.g., Mistral) for different purposes like query rewriting, earning 30 points. Otari features: web search/fetch (10), code execution (10), multiple models in distinct roles (10), model routing (10) = 40 points. Working app with real use case (5) and clear video (5) = 10 points. Total 80.

ideas.title: AI-Powered Code Review Bot with Guardrails
ideas.pitch: A solo developer who wants to improve code quality can integrate this bot into their GitHub workflow; it uses an open-weight model to review pull requests, applies guardrails to avoid suggesting insecure code, and uses per-user budgets to limit usage per contributor. The demo wow moment: showing a PR review that catches a security flaw and explains it safely.
ideas.rationale: Uses one open-weight model (e.g., CodeLlama) for reviews, earning 20 points. Otari features: guardrails (10), per-user budgets (10), MCP integrations (10), model routing (10) = 40 points. Working app (5) + video (5) = 10. Total 70.

ideas.title: Personal Finance Advisor with Budget Tracking
ideas.pitch: A user wanting to manage expenses can chat with this agent that uses an open-weight model to analyze spending patterns, sets per-user budgets via Otari, and uses web fetch to get current exchange rates or stock prices. The demo wow moment: the agent warns 'You've exceeded your dining budget this month' and suggests cheaper alternatives.
ideas.rationale: Uses two open-weight models (e.g., Llama for chat, another for analysis) earning 30 points. Otari features: budgets (10), per-user budgets (10), web fetch (10) = 30 points. Working app (5) + video (5) = 10. Total 70.

ideas.title: Code Review Buddy
ideas.pitch: A solo developer often pushes code without a second pair of eyes. This agent reviews pull requests by fetching the diff via web fetch, running code execution to test snippets, and using an open-weight model to flag bugs and style issues. The demo wow moment: it catches a subtle off-by-one error and suggests a fix live.
ideas.rationale: Uses one open-weight model (20 pts) plus code execution and web fetch (20 pts) for a total of 40, but no second model or other features. Demo is clear and useful.

ideas.title: Personal Research Assistant
ideas.pitch: A student or researcher needs to quickly gather and summarize information from multiple sources. This agent uses web search to find articles, an open-weight model to summarize each, and a second open-weight model to synthesize a final report with citations. The demo wow moment: it answers a complex query with a concise, cited summary in seconds.
ideas.rationale: Uses two open-weight models (30 pts) and web search (10 pts) for 40, but no other features. Demo is compelling and practical.

ideas.title: Budget-Conscious Chatbot
ideas.pitch: A small business owner wants an AI customer support chatbot without overspending. This agent uses model routing to fallback from a powerful open-weight model to a cheaper one when budgets are tight, and enforces per-user budgets to prevent abuse. The demo wow moment: it shows a user hitting their daily limit and the bot politely declining, then routing to a cheaper model for another user.
ideas.rationale: Uses one open-weight model (20 pts) plus routing, budgets, per-user budgets, and guardrails (40 pts) for 60. Demo is clear but less flashy.

ideas.title: AI‑Powered Personal Knowledge Base Summarizer
ideas.pitch: A solo developer can finish a personal knowledge‑base app that lets users paste articles or notes and instantly get concise, bullet‑point summaries and Q&A pairs. The agent routes queries to a summarizer model (Llama‑2‑7B) or a Q&A model (Mistral‑7B) and falls back to a smaller distilled model if latency spikes, while guardrails prevent hallucinations.
ideas.rationale: open_weight_models: uses two distinct open‑weight models for different tasks (20 pts → 8/10). otari_features: implements model routing/fallbacks, guardrails, per‑user budgets, and web fetch for citation retrieval (4 features → 6/10). project_demo: a working web UI with a 30‑second demo video showing a before/after summary (5 pts each → 6/10).

ideas.title: Smart Email Draft Assistant
ideas.pitch: An email‑drafting side‑project that auto‑generates professional replies based on tone, context, and user‑defined style guides. Otari routes the email body to a tone‑analysis model (Open‑Chat‑3.5) and then to a generation model (Phi‑2) while applying per‑user budgets and a simple guardrail to block sensitive content.
ideas.rationale: open_weight_models: two open‑weight models (summarizer + style guide) – 18 pts → 7/10. otari_features: uses multiple models, per‑user budgets, and guardrails (3 features) – 30 pts → 5/10. project_demo: functional Chrome extension demo with a 45‑second screen‑recorded walkthrough – 10 pts → 5/10.

ideas.title: AI Travel Planner with Real‑time Info
ideas.pitch: A travel‑planning app that creates day‑by‑day itineraries, fetches live flight/hotel prices, and suggests activities. Otari orchestrates a route‑planning model (Mistral‑7B) and a price‑prediction model (Llama‑2‑13B), uses web search/fetch for live data, MCP integration for map display, and guardrails to keep suggestions family‑friendly.
ideas.rationale: open_weight_models: two open‑weight models for itinerary generation and price prediction – 20 pts → 8/10. otari_features: employs model routing/fallbacks, web search/fetch, MCP (map) integration, guardrails, and multiple‑model roles (5 features) – 50 pts → 7/10. project_demo: end‑to‑end demo where a user inputs a destination and sees a live, interactive itinerary with price links – 10 pts → 7/10.

ideas.title: Personal Knowledge Base Assistant
ideas.pitch: A browser extension that lets users ask natural‑language questions about their saved notes, PDFs, and web clippings. It uses an embedding model to retrieve relevant chunks and a generation model to answer, showing a live demo where a user asks a multi‑step question and gets a concise, sourced response.
ideas.rationale: Open‑weight models: uses two distinct models (embedding + generation) meaningfully (20 pts +10 pts). Otari features: employs model routing, web fetch for PDFs, budgets, guardrails, per‑user budgets, and multiple‑model roles (≈35 pts). Demo: functional Chrome extension with a short screencast (5 pts). Total ≈70/100 → 7‑8/10.

ideas.title: GitHub PR Code Review Bot
ideas.pitch: A GitHub Action that automatically reviews pull requests, flags potential bugs, suggests improvements, and can run safe code snippets. The wow moment is a live PR where the bot comments with a detailed review and a runnable example fixing a lint error.
ideas.rationale: Open‑weight models: uses a code‑focused LLM for analysis and a general LLM for explanations (20 pts +10 pts). Otari features: MCP integration (GitHub), code execution sandbox, model routing, budgets, guardrails, multiple‑model roles, per‑user budgets (≈45 pts). Demo: fully functional Action with a recorded PR walkthrough (5 pts). Total ≈80/100 → 8/10.

ideas.title: Real‑time Travel Itinerary Planner
ideas.pitch: A web app where users type a destination and dates, and the AI builds a day‑by‑day itinerary, fetching live flight and hotel prices. The demo shows the app generating an itinerary and instantly updating prices when the user tweaks travel dates.
ideas.rationale: Open‑weight models: one LLM for itinerary generation and a lightweight retrieval model for price lookup (20 pts +10 pts). Otari features: web search/fetch, model routing, budgets, guardrails, multiple‑model roles, per‑user budgets (≈35 pts). Demo: working UI with live data fetch and AI‑generated plan (5 pts). Total ≈70/100 → 7/10.
